about.heading: About
content: I am a Paris-based scenographer and French state-certified architect, originally from China. My practice explores the intersection between architecture and performance, with a particular focus on how space, light, and movement can shape narrative and perception.

I was trained in architecture at ENSA Paris-Malaquais and China Central Academy of Fine Arts, where I developed a strong foundation in spatial design and project management, and later completed a degree in scenography at Sorbonne Nouvelle and École Duperré. This dual background allows me to approach projects at different scales, from built environments to stage design, always with attention to both concept and execution.

Professionally, I have worked as an architect and project manager, coordinating with clients and engineering teams on complex projects. At the same time, I expanded my practice into the performing arts through internships in the lighting departments of the Odéon Théâtre de l'Europe and Théâtre des Champs-Élysées, as well as within the design office of the Opéra national de Paris. These experiences strengthened my understanding of technical constraints while deepening my interest in atmosphere, dramaturgy, and the expressive potential of light.

My approach is both rigorous and intuitive, combining technical precision with a sensitivity to visual storytelling. I am interested in creating spaces that are not only functional, but also immersive and evocative, where architecture becomes a medium for experience.
Outside of my professional work, I draw inspiration from opera, dance, and visual arts, which continue to inform my approach to rhythm, composition, and scenographic thinking.

items.title: The Winter's Tale
items.desc:
This play is one of Shakespeare's final works, blending tragedy and comedy. In the end, the lost daughter is found, the lovers are reunited, and Leontes is forgiven. Yet this return to harmony feels almost too sudden, raising the question of whether such forgiveness was truly believable for audiences.

The story unfolds between two imagined worlds: Sicily, a palace bound by the rules and appearances of power, and Bohemia, a pastoral utopia filled with joyful peasants and abundant nature. After Time's monologue, the play shifts into a lighter, almost magical tone. Yet in the end, the lovers must leave Bohemia and return to Sicily to find peace, subtly questioning the idea of utopia.

This paradox interests me. Can the stage itself become an imaginary utopia—a place where anything is possible? At the same time, the Italian-style theatre reflects a strict spatial hierarchy, almost like a monarchy. I also explore Leontes' madness through the image of a labyrinth, representing his disordered thoughts and inviting the audience to experience his shifting state of mind through scenography.

items.title: Quai Ouest
items.desc:
For me, Quai Ouest is a play that deeply questions the notion of limits—physical, moral, and existential. What interests me most are the gestures of the characters at the moment of choosing—or not choosing. At every instant, they are confronted with a decision: to cross or not to cross, to leave or to stay, to live or to die.

Koch arrives intending to end his life, yet retreats, paralyzed by fear. Monique wants to leave from the very beginning, but remains until the end. Cécile constantly complains, yet never truly decides. Charles finally says goodbye to Rodolphe, but death comes before he can act. All hesitate to cross the threshold, to commit to a decisive gesture. And while they waver, death appears—sudden, unpredictable, and without dialogue.

The only figure who fully acts, without words, is Abad—a silent character whose body carries out the ultimate gesture: to kill. He embodies the boundary itself, acting where others remain frozen.

Through these unresolved trajectories, Koltès exposes the complexity of the human condition—its inability to choose, to move freely, caught within inner, social, and existential conflicts. The play reveals those suspended moments where one either crosses into action—or does not—into the irreversible. And it is within these often thwarted or aborted gestures that the full tension of the piece resides.

items.title: Loewe X Ghibli Window Display
items.desc: Light as a second body on stage. Precise control of beam angles, colour temperature, and shadow geometry to sculpt the sensation of weight and weightlessness.

items.title: Hermes Window Display - The Winter's Tale
items.desc:
The Winter's Tale inspired Hermes window display series draws from the poetic worlds of the story, transforming the store windows into theatrical landscapes of imagination and travel. Each scene evokes a chapter through handcrafted paper sets, where architecture, nature, and stage-like compositions create a sense of wonder and narrative.

Within these dreamlike environments, Hermes objects appear as precious discoveries, highlighting the craftsmanship while inviting viewers into a visual journey between theatre, fantasy, and storytelling.

items.title: Hermes Window Display - Year of the Goat
items.desc: A jumping sheep leads us to the year of goat.

items.title: Monument Valley
items.desc:
Located in a valley crossed by a river, the Ninfeo Bramante is hidden near the center of the town. It is one of the most well-known architectural landmarks for its Renaissance style. However, the monument has not been well preserved: the structure has been deformed over time, and graffiti can be found on some walls. This project aims to transform the ruin into a theater surrounded by a garden.

The original project was conceived as a quiet place to rest during the summer, but it was never completed. Therefore, we decided to preserve its classical and natural atmosphere. We created an axis that extends from the center of the hall toward the garden. This axis begins at the entrance: standing in front of the door, visitors can see the entire landscape through the central arch. Finally, a rectangular pool guides the view toward nature. The main path includes a gift shop and a sequence of passages that alternate between indoor and outdoor spaces. As visitors walk through the ruins, a "dark box" is placed along the descent toward the garden. Inside this box, there is only a small window facing the lower part of the river. Once on the ground floor, the architecture opens completely toward the garden. Visitors do not need to enter the building to admire the interior, which reveals a dialogue between new materials and historical traces.

We conceived three different configurations for the theater in order to accommodate various types of performances: one for small plays, one for concerts, and a temporary configuration for large-scale performances such as theater festivals or opera. In addition, there is an outdoor stage located in the center of the garden. Actors perform in front of the pool, while the audience sits on the slightly elevated lawn facing the stage. Thanks to these flexible uses, the theater can operate efficiently both during the day and at night.

Several small structures were designed to connect the different parts of the garden, including a broken pilaster from the existing architecture. The proposal encourages visitors to explore the garden through minimal interventions. We believe that this project will bring new life to the Renaissance ruin while providing a high-quality performance space for both visitors and local residents.

items.title: Rehabilitation of Saint-Ouen Flea Market
items.desc:
The Saint-Ouen Flea Market, located north of Paris, is composed of seven distinct markets. The construction of the Paris ring road divided the urban fabric and exposed many buildings along its edge. Unlike planned developments, the flea market grew spontaneously over time, forming a collection of individual markets established mainly in the late 20th century.

In this context, the project proposes a top-down spatial system that reflects the historical presence of the ring road while creating a physical connection within this bottom-up commercial community. The goal is to improve circulation, visibility, and shared public spaces.

For local residents, the main concern is not tourism but safety. Interviews with inhabitants revealed that some poorly organized spaces between markets have become gathering points and are not clearly used by merchants, tourists, or residents. The project therefore reorganizes these open spaces to improve accessibility and everyday use.

For visitors, navigating the seven markets without guidance can be difficult. The proposed system helps identify each market and guides visitors through the community's open spaces. Integrated into the existing urban fabric and running parallel to the ring road, the intervention adapts to each market's structure, sometimes creating new entrances and connections.

For example, the Biron Market, previously accessible only from its two ends, gains additional access points. At Serpette Market, the rooftop parking area is transformed into a public space connected to a newly created courtyard. These interventions create new pathways, improving circulation for both tourists and local residents.

items.title: Bobigny - L’Histoire Sur Une Dalle
items.desc:
Since the 1960s, slab urbanism in Paris has served as a field of experimentation where urban layers are separated, recomposed, and reinterpreted. Projects such as Les Olympiades, Front de Seine, and Montparnasse embody this ambition to stack flows, liberate the ground plane, and invent new forms of inhabitation. Suspended between modernist utopia and contemporary critique, these urban structures oscillate between fragmentation and intensified use.

Bobigny-La Folie represents an extreme condition of this stratification: a node where heterogeneous infrastructures converge, including the canal, road network, metro, and tramway, producing a dense and complex territorial thickness. Here, the ground is no longer continuous, but fragmented into a succession of planes, thresholds, and discontinuities.

The project proposes to engage this thickness by connecting the different levels, not through simple superposition, but through a logic of inhabited continuity. The slab becomes a mediating device, capable of articulating circulation and use.

Structured by a modular grid, the project introduces a degree of programmatic indeterminacy in which public facilities, commercial spaces, and housing coexist within an evolving system. Spatial reversibility becomes a key principle, allowing the project to remain open-ended and adaptable in response to future urban transformations.

items.title: Cube
items.desc: A modular structure composed of 64 cubic units, integrating living, working, and exhibition spaces, located within the historic hutong district of Beijing. Two and a half levels rise above ground, while the rest are embedded below. Designed to be fully demountable, each unit can function independently and be placed within public spaces. Its bamboo-steel structure ensures lightness and ease of mobility.

items.title: Plug-In
items.desc:
Roubaix bears the traces of a brutal deindustrialization, marked by the decline of the textile industry and the lasting weakening of its urban and social fabric. In a dense city center, where possibilities for expansion are limited, the question is no longer how to build more, but how to reveal the potentials already embedded within the existing city.

The long and narrow plot structure, characterized by significant depth, produces underused block interiors. These voids, invisible from public space, constitute a latent resource.

The project proposes a plug-in strategy designed to activate these interstitial spaces. By linking plots together, it introduces new low-cost student housing while relying on the existing urban fabric. Rooftops become a collective ground plane, transforming the block interior into a shared space.

This urban graft makes it possible to densify without demolition, create new forms of sociability, and generate complementary economic value for local residents.

items.title: A Villa In Mountains
items.desc: A two-story residence nestled in the mountainous outskirts of Beijing.

items.title: Underground Light
items.desc:
As the capital of China, Beijing has long attracted a large population of migrant workers with relatively higher wages. Many of them are employed in low-end sectors and, to reduce living costs, often reside in poorly conditioned basements. On November 18, 2017, a major basement fire caused 19 deaths and 8 injuries. In response, the city launched a 40-day safety campaign, leading to the eviction of many migrant residents from underground spaces. Since then, numerous basements once used for housing have remained vacant.

The question of how to repurpose these spaces has since emerged. Initiatives such as Digua Community have explored ways to transform them into much-needed public facilities, offering services to local residents in a city lacking communal spaces.

This project is located on the basement level of a residential building, characterized by a large and complex layout. By introducing an artificial lighting atmosphere along the main circulation path and embracing the inherent darkness of the space, I reorganized it into three distinct zones, each providing different types of community-oriented services.

items.title: Private Apartment
items.desc: Complete interior of a 80sqm apartment. The brief called for restraint: a home that feels quietly refined, where every surface and joint is considered.

items.title: INSIDE - Festival Everybody
items.desc:
This project is inspired by a bodily exploration of the intestines—essential yet often overlooked organs that work continuously inside our bodies. Although largely invisible, they play a fundamental role in everyday life. In this installation, the intestines become a metaphor for transformation: they digest and assimilate, just as we constantly process emotions, experiences, and our surrounding environment.

The installation is composed of stretched threads forming an organic labyrinth that evokes the inner structures of the body. Inspired by the apparent disorder of organic tissues, the space reveals a hidden order within irregularity. Bathed in deep purple tones and animated by light and texture, this immersive architecture invites visitors to move through a sensory environment and reconnect with their inner world.

items.title: Wood Pavillon

items.title: Just Another Creation Myth
items.desc: This poster was designed for a show in which I participated as a set designer. Created before the construction of the set, it combines reference images with the atmosphere of the performance to produce a manifesto image that captures the visual identity of the project.

items.title: CAFArch 2015 Show

items.title: Floating
items.desc: This series of screen prints is inspired by a dream in which I felt as if I were floating inside a bottle of eye drops. The mint essence created a refreshing sensation, evoking the calm of a summer moment. In this work, I imagine a scaled world where a human figure floats inside everyday objects, transforming ordinary spaces into surreal environments.

items.title: Louis Vuitton Conquest
items.desc:
Today, online shopping has become an essential part of everyday life. Products ordered online can be delivered within days, supported by global infrastructures connecting the world through maritime routes and air traffic. These networks reveal how closely our economies and societies are interconnected.

Based on this context, we analyzed the brand Louis Vuitton, the French luxury fashion house known for its iconic logo and high-end products. Our research explored its branding, marketing strategies, and its strong dependence on maritime transport, as well as its historical connections to colonial trade and global capitalism. Inspired by board games such as Monopoly and War, we created a game that narrates the history of Louis Vuitton, inviting players to discover how its commercial empire was established and expanded.

items.title: Louis Vuitton Express
items.desc: Louis Vuitton is a luxury brand that offers almost everything a wealthy lifestyle might require. Today, however, the meaning of luxury is evolving: the possession of goods is no longer the only symbol of wealth. The ability to travel quickly and reach new horizons has become a new form of luxury. Based on this idea, we imagined a rocket service through which Louis Vuitton could take its clients on a journey to the Moon.

items.title: Paris Plage II
items.desc: Parisien cafe used to heating outside terrasse for that people can enjoy outside space in winter, but it caused a lot of energy consumption. Heating the cold for warmth is not a sustainable solution. So I came up with this ironic concept to warning people about the environmental impact of such practices.
